obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived scoped relation; finite observations do not establish a general proof.
obernants.assumptions: Named tests are finite observations: residual sides 128/129 activate sorting, 127 retains scanning, and 81 integer 2x2 matrices exercise the assignment relation. Reservation-failure and overflow fallback may remain source-local rather than forced by this harness. Equality of scalar optimal values does not imply equality of tied assignment vectors. Nonfinite/ragged and malformed partition semantics remain outside this evidence.
obernants.domain: Finite well-formed mention spans with stable order, shared matching-key groups and controlled exact/residual overlap construction. Assignment cases are finite rectangular matrices, including empty and negative cases. The integer oracle relation additionally requires exact integer conversion and safe negation; noninteger input is rejected by that relation rather than by the unrestricted float API.
obernants.observation_scope: Test-observation joins only: actual matcher output identities are checked against explicit policy expectations and actual heap-sorted total keys; actual float maximum assignment objectives are checked against independent integer minimum-assignment and enumerated objectives on their common domain. assign_max is not installed inside the greedy matcher. The algorithm-library nodes remain in their existing hierarchy.
obernants.operator: The bounded observation universe excludes reporting the optimum 8 as the greedy result for the leading [[5,4],[4,0]] case, allowing residual overlap to displace exact matches, and reversing zero-overlap ties. For the integer adapter it excludes accepting an unrepresentable fractional matrix as an exact integer comparison. These are different tagged exclusions, not one shared optimizer specification.
